title: Batch snapshot pocket - quick ledger
content:
Purpose:
Quick pocket ledger to capture short batch-snapshot runs I'm eyeballing. Not formal; meant for quick decision-making and triage before I promote any config to a bench dashboard.

Table - recent micro-batch snapshots (most recent at top):
date,exp_id,model_variant,batch_size,avg_latency_ms,p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_per_call,cost_per_1k_tokens,notes
2026-02-26,bs-276-g,redwood-7b-q4_ggml,8,42,29,98,820,0.32,"prefix caching ON, KV reuse decent; tail p95 wobble on long prompts (~1k+)."
2026-02-25,bs-275-f,redwood-13b-int8,4,76,61,163,1400,0.54,"single-tenant node; batching overhead visible at <=4, try 6 next."
2026-02-20,bs-270-d,redwood-7b-q4_ggml,16,88,55,245,560,0.18,"high throughput but p95 climbs; observed GPU mem spikes when concurrent sessions >3."
2026-01-15,bs-248-a,mpt-7b-chat-int4,12,95,70,230,1100,0.20,"cheap per-token but slow kernel for fwd-only attention; quant artifacts noticed in eval set A."
2025-12-02,bs-201-x,redwood-70b-fp16,1,350,320,410,4000,3.40,"baseline for QA. Good quality, expensive; test half-precision kernel cut cost by ~10%."
2025-11-21,bs-198-z,redwood-13b-int8,8,128,115,202,950,0.62,"burst config with async IO; retry rates low."

Quick notes / heuristics observed:
- Batch size sweet spot appears model-dependent: 7b variants like 8-16 deliver best unit cost but p95 can explode if prompts >800 tokens. Keep TTL cache to avoid regen.
- For 13b-int8, single-digit batching (4-8) reduces tail more than increasing batch to 12. Might be due to kernel scheduling latency.
- Where latency SLO is hard (<=100ms p95), prefer smaller batches + prefix cache + faster quant profile even if cost slightly higher.

Hypotheses to validate (short list):
- H1: Enabling preemptive KV flushing every 10s reduces p95 spikes for small-batch heavy-concurrent workloads. (plan: run bs-280 with and without, 1h window)
- H2: Async IO buffer size of 256KB vs 128KB improves throughput for 13b on gfx-xx nodes by ~6% (plan: A/B bs-282)

Things I noticed that require follow-up:
- Two failures on 2026-02-25 run: one OOM on host (node l3b) and one transient socket timeout -> link to INF-1183.
- Prompt set B (customer-sim) shows hallucination uptick when using int4 profile on MPT; record examples and file with eval harness.

Immediate next actions (today):
- Run bs-283: redwood-7b-q4_ggml at batch=12 with KV TTL=15s, 30m window (Jules)
- Add bs-275-f (13b-int8) run at batch=6 with increased async buffer (Maya)
- Create quick eval slice for prompt set B and dump 50 failure examples to /tmp/promptB-fails (Samir)

Scratch math (guesstimates):
- If avg tokens/call ~820 and cost_per_1k_tokens=0.32 => cost per call ~0.2624 USD. At 1000 calls/day that's ~$262/day for this config. Useful for comparing with 13b-int8 which sits ~0.54/1k.

Random TODOs (non-blocking):
- Cross-check bs-270-d mem spikes with node-level metrics (SRE)
- Add a tiny column to the main bench dashboard: "concurrent_sessions" to better correlate p95
- Try quant profile v2 (blend-int) next week on 7b variant

Notes-to-self style (messy):
- If I can't reduce p95 w/kv tweaks, try moving to dedicated smaller GPU (lower node queuing) or enable fallback to cheaper quick-mode model for tail requests.
- Keep this pocket ledger short; when one config stabilizes, promote to eng-applied-ml/batches/bench-uploads.

References/links:
- GH PR: repo/infer-runtime#472 (scheduling tweaks)
- JIRA INF-1183 (OOM/tracing)
- Slack thread: #runtime-bench tXw9

End of pocket ledger.
